content: For fountains, a facility will be classified as an interactive recreational water facility (RWF) if there is any piping connected through a recirculation system. These facilities may have zero water depth. Fully or partially enclosed water slides are also considered interactive recreational water facilities. The term keel laying refers to the date when construction identifiable with a specific ship begins, and when the assembly of that ship comprises at least 50 tons or 1% of the estimated mass of all structural material, whichever is less. The unit mg/L stands for milligrams per liter, which is the metric equivalent of parts per million (ppm). The term noncorroding describes a material that retains its original surface characteristics despite prolonged exposure to environmental conditions, food contact, and the normal use of cleaning agents and sanitizing solutions. Nonfood-contact surfaces (nonfood zones) refer to all exposed surfaces of equipment located in food areas, excluding food-contact surfaces. Permeate water lines are pipes that carry permeate water from the reverse osmosis unit, which may be directed to the potable water system. This is the Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) definition for pipe striping purposes. The term pH (potential hydrogen) represents the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration, which measures the acidity or alkalinity of a solution. Values between 0 and 7 indicate acidity, while values between 7 and 14 indicate alkalinity. A pH of 7, as in pure distilled water, is neutral. A plumbing fixture is a receptacle or device that is either permanently or temporarily connected to the vessel's water distribution system and requires a water supply, or it discharges used water, waste materials, or sewage directly or indirectly into the vessel's drainage system. The term portable describes equipment that is easily removable, mounted on casters, gliders, or rollers, or equipped with a mechanical means to tilt it safely for cleaning. It can also be moved by one person. A pressure vacuum breaker assembly (PVB) is a device consisting of an independently loaded internal check valve and a spring-loaded air inlet valve. It also includes two resilient seated gate valves and test cocks. The term readily accessible refers to surfaces that are exposed or can be exposed for cleaning or inspection without the use of tools. The term readily removable refers to components that can be detached from the main unit without the use of tools. Recreational seawater refers to seawater taken onboard while the vessel is underway at least 12 miles from shore. This water is routed directly to recreational water facilities (RWFs) for either sea-to-sea exchange or recirculation. A recreational water facility (RWF) is a water facility that has been modified, improved, constructed, or installed for public swimming or recreational bathing. Examples of RWFs include activity pools, baby-only water facilities, children's pools, diving pools, hot tubs, hydrotherapy pools, interactive recreational water facilities, slides, spa pools, swimming pools, therapeutic pools, wading pools, and whirlpools. A reduced pressure principle backflow prevention assembly (RP assembly) is a device containing two independently acting, internally loaded check valves, along with a hydraulically operating, mechanically independent pressure differential relief valve located between the check valves and below the first check valve. The unit must include properly located resilient seated test cocks and tightly closing resilient seated shutoff valves at each end of the assembly. The term removable refers to components that can be detached from the main unit using simple tools such as a screwdriver, pliers, or an open-end wrench. A safety vacuum release system (SVRS) is a system capable of releasing a vacuum at a suction outlet caused by high vacuum due to a blockage in the outlet flow. Sanitary seawater lines are water lines carrying seawater intended for use in potable water production systems or recreational water facilities. A scupper is a conduit or collection basin that channels liquid runoff to a deck drain. Sealant refers to a material used to fill seams that are 8 millimeters (1/32 inch) or less but greater than 3 millimeters (1/8 inch). The term smooth is defined as follows: For food-contact surfaces, it refers to a surface free of pits and inclusions, with cleanability equal to or exceeding that of 100-grit number 3 stainless steel. For nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment, it refers to a surface equivalent to commercial-grade hot-rolled steel, free of visible scale. For decks, bulkheads, or deckheads, it refers to an even or level surface with no roughness or projections that would make cleaning difficult. A spa pool is a pool supplied with potable water or saltwater, with temperatures and turbulence comparable to a whirlpool spa. It has a depth of more than 1 meter (3 feet) and a tub volume exceeding 6 tons of water. A spill-resistant vacuum breaker (SVB) is a specific modification to a pressure vacuum breaker assembly designed to minimize water spillage. A spray pad is a play and water contact area designed to have no standing water.
